To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) non-NaCl crystallisation conditions were used to eliminate partial conversion between cisplatin and carboplatin; (ii) two molecules of carbplatin bind to His-15 after 5 weeks of crystal growth, and (iii) a new resolution limit criterion was used to process the X-ray diffraction to 2.3Å.

(i) non-NaCl crystallisation conditions of carbaplatin showed a carboplastic molecule bound to His15 of HEWL after 1 week of crystal growth, whereas after 5 weeks of crystal growth, two carboplatin molecules were bound; (ii) the use of several different criteria for the resolution limit of the X-ray data, led to the successful processing of the data to higher resolution than was originally thought.

- non-NaCl co-crystallization conditions were used to eliminate partial conversion from carboplatin to its isomer cisplatin in the crystals; - the resolution limit of the X-ray diffraction pattern was determined using several criteria and the resolution was found to be 2-2.2A; and - the structural data showed one carboplatin molecule binding to the His-115 residue after one week and two carboplatin molecules after five weeks of growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the binding of platinum drugs to model proteins.
the use of carboplatin as a model drug to study the mechanism of action of platinum drugs.
the binding of carboplatin and cisplatin to the protein hen egg white lysozye (HEWL).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
non-NaCl co-crystallization conditions of carboplastic with HEWL have been utilised successfully, and that a resolution limit of the data to 2.3Å has been determined.
the CC1/2 and the Rfree values were the best criteria for determining the data resolution limit.

the use of non-NaCl carboplatin conditions led to a single carboplatin molecule binding to the Nδ binding position of HEWL, whereas two carboplatin molecules bound to the His 15 residue of HEWL after 5 weeks of crystal growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully used non-NaCl HEWL co-crystallization conditions to eliminate partial cisplatin conversion, and have used several criteria to determine a higher resolution limit.
we have successfully obtained a crystal structure of carboplatin bound at the His-15 site of HEWL, and have used several criteria to determine a diffraction resolution limit.

the use of non-NaCl co-crystallising conditions for carboplatin and HEWL has been successfully used, and that the use of multiple criteria for choosing the resolution limit for model refinement has led to a more robust model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of several different criteria to determine the resolution limit is a useful strategy to obtain higher resolution data.
it is not always necessary to use the CC1/2 criteria implemented in the XDS software package.
the CC1/2 and FreeR value criteria should be used together to determine the diffractions resolution limit, and that the EVAL software package can also be used to determine the resolution limit.
